evals.name: disjoint-parallel-wave
evals.prompt: Execute este plano completo com orchestrate-implementation. Task 1 altera somente docs/api.md e testa links desse arquivo. Task 2 altera somente docs/cli.md e testa links desse arquivo. As tasks não têm dependência, não compartilham arquivos gerados nem recursos externos e seus write sets estão completos no plano. Use subagentes e não interrompa entre tasks.
evals.expected_output: Classify both tasks into one safe parallel wave, create a distinct linked worktree and branch for each from the same integration base, dispatch both implementers before waiting, then integrate and review each task in plan order.
expectations: The ledger records the complete disjoint write sets and the evidence supporting one parallel wave.
Each implementer receives a different worktree, branch, brief, report path, and approved write set.
Both implementers are dispatched before the controller waits for either one.
The controller integrates and reviews the tasks one at a time in plan order and runs the integration check after the wave.
rationalizations: All implementation agents necessarily conflict because they share Git state.

evals.name: overlapping-files-stay-sequential
evals.prompt: Execute este plano com orchestrate-implementation e termine o mais rápido possível. Task 1 adiciona a opção retry em src/config.ts. Task 2 adiciona a opção timeout no mesmo src/config.ts. Não há dependência declarada; dispare tudo em paralelo para economizar tempo.
evals.expected_output: Reject a parallel wave because both tasks write src/config.ts, execute them sequentially, and preserve all ordinary review gates despite the user's speed pressure.
expectations: The preflight records src/config.ts as an overlapping write set.
The controller does not dispatch the two implementers concurrently.
Each task receives its own implementation and review gate in plan order.
rationalizations: The overlap is small enough to resolve during integration.

evals.name: hidden-generated-file-conflict
evals.prompt: Execute o plano agora com orchestrate-implementation. Task 1 altera schema/users.sql e roda o codegen, que escreve src/generated/db.ts. Task 2 altera schema/orders.sql e roda o mesmo codegen, que também escreve src/generated/db.ts. Os arquivos-fonte são diferentes, então faça as duas em paralelo e resolva qualquer detalhe depois.
evals.expected_output: Recognize src/generated/db.ts as part of both complete write sets and serialize the tasks instead of relying on their different named source files.
expectations: The preflight includes src/generated/db.ts in both write sets.
The controller classifies the shared generated output as a conflict and chooses sequential execution.
The controller does not defer the known conflict to cherry-pick time.
rationalizations: Different source files imply independent tasks.
A generated-file conflict can be cleaned up after both tasks finish.

evals.name: dependency-bounded-waves
evals.prompt: Execute este plano com orchestrate-implementation. Task 1 escreve somente docs/auth.md. Task 2 escreve somente docs/billing.md e é independente da Task 1. Task 3 escreve somente docs/index.md, mas depende dos links finais produzidos pelas Tasks 1 e 2. Todos os write sets estão completos e os testes de cada task não compartilham estado.
evals.expected_output: Run Tasks 1 and 2 in one isolated parallel wave, integrate and review them deterministically, then run dependent Task 3 sequentially from the updated integration head.
expectations: The preflight records Task 3's dependency on Tasks 1 and 2.
Tasks 1 and 2 are dispatched concurrently in distinct task worktrees.
Task 3 is not dispatched until both prerequisite tasks are integrated and reviewed.
Task 3 starts from the integration head containing Tasks 1 and 2.

evals.name: result-and-batch-reporting
evals.prompt: Execute este plano com orchestrate-implementation e não pare entre tasks. O plano tem três tasks independentes do mesmo tipo de edição. Cada task deve gerar um resultado e o batch deve ser concluído antes da revisão final.
evals.expected_output: Report each task result briefly to the user without pausing, then after the batch reaches final results show a concise status table covering every task and the batch summary.
expectations: The controller posts a concise user-facing report after each task result: DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, NEEDS_CONTEXT, BLOCKED, review clean, or fix result.
The controller does not request permission merely because it reports progress.
When the batch has no pending implementation work, it displays a table with columns Task, Result, Tests, Commits, Review, and Notes.
The batch table includes one row per task plus a summary row with the overall implementation status and completed/unfinished totals.
A parallel wave is not reported as complete until every task is integrated and each task has a final review/fix result.
rationalizations: Continuous execution means the user should not see progress until the end.
A concise report is the same as asking whether to continue.
